title: 2 Chronicles 28:1–4
context: Ahaz reigns sixteen years and does not do what is right like David. He walks in the ways of Israel’s kings, makes molten images for the Baals, burns incense in the valley of the son of Hinnom, and burns his children in the fire. The parallel in 2 Kings 16:2-4 says he made his son pass through the fire; Chronicles speaks of his children and names the valley. Both books name this sacrifice as one of the abominations of the nations the LORD drove out, and the notes treat it with the same plain grief as 2 Kings 16:3 and 17:17.

verses.text: Ahaz was twenty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. He didn’t do that which was right in the LORD’s eyes, like David his father,
verses.arminianNotes: Ahaz reigns sixteen years and does not do right like David. Arminian readers see a sharp turn from the faithful examples of his father and grandfather, a turn he freely chose.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that the verdict matches 2 Kings 16:2. Ahaz is measured against David, the standard for the kings of Judah, and found wanting from the start.

verses.text: but he walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, and also made molten images for the Baals.
verses.arminianNotes: He walks in the ways of Israel’s kings and makes molten images for the Baals. Arminian readers see a king of Judah adopting the very worship that had already brought judgment on the northern kingdom.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that the molten images for the Baals are named only in Chronicles; 2 Kings 16:3 speaks of the way of the kings of Israel. Judah’s king imports what the prophets had condemned in the north.

verses.text: Moreover he burned incense in the valley of the son of Hinnom, and burned his children in the fire, according to the abominations of the nations whom the LORD cast out before the children of Israel.
verses.arminianNotes: Ahaz burned his children in the fire in the valley of the son of Hinnom. Arminian readers name this plainly as child sacrifice, forbidden in Deuteronomy 18:10, and they grieve for the children, as in the notes on 2 Kings 16:3 and 17:17.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers grieve with the text over this abomination of the nations the LORD drove out. Chronicles speaks of his children, while 2 Kings 16:3 says his son; the valley of Hinnom is named only here, and it later becomes a symbol of judgment (Jeremiah 7:31-32).

verses.text: He sacrificed and burned incense in the high places, and on the hills, and under every green tree.
verses.arminianNotes: He sacrifices on the high places, on the hills, and under every green tree. Arminian readers see worship scattered across the land, each site a fresh choice to turn from the LORD’s appointed place.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that the verse matches 2 Kings 16:4 nearly word for word. The language recalls the Deuteronomic command to destroy such places (Deuteronomy 12:2), which Ahaz instead multiplied.
